literal_implementation_scope.constraints: No controller.py protocol declaration, receiver/workflow/dispatch changes, policy expansion, model/source tool, endpoint, generic SQL/table/callback/path argument, self_host edits, question/answer handling, owner command, UI/harness/renderer/package change, authority cleanup, or operational state mutation. No ambient sys.path/import fallback, caller-selected module/path/table/SQL/callback, source-agent tool or authority expansion. The complete fixed module split is allowed for cohesion; omit an unused named module rather than creating filler, and add no further production module without a plan revision. Keep the public API/error facades on review_control, shared exception identity within the loaded closure, and unchanged legacy functions/signatures/results. Tests enter through those facades with actual disposable SQLite and inert GitHub objects. Keep cohesive tests below500 lines and strictly below700 each; use small helper functions to meet existing lint/complexity policy, never refresh quality-debt baselines.

canonical_encoding_and_bounds.canonical_json: C(value) is UTF8 of json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False); H(value)=SHA256(C(value)). No default coercion, custom encoder, repr-based hashing, Unicode normalization or omission of null/empty fields. Accept exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None types only; EVERY dictionary key must be an exact built-in str before sorting/encoding, including opaque profile_sources/execution.identity metadata. No integer/bool/None/tuple/custom key coercion or dict/list/str subclass is accepted. Finite float is permitted only inside hash-bound opaque receipt metadata, never for identities, revisions, counts or caller fields. Reject reference cycles before encoding; repeated noncyclic shared values are counted at each occurrence. Duplicate JSON keys are rejected if decoding a string/byte fixture. Public inputs are already structured objects, not an arbitrary document parser.
canonical_encoding_and_bounds.legacy_binding_encoding: L(binding)=UTF8 of the existing json.dumps(binding, sort_keys=True) with its existing default ASCII escaping and spaces. Compare the actual coordinator_holds.binding SQL TEXT byte-for-byte with L(binding). Binding SHA used in checked receipt keys is SHA256(L(binding)), not H(binding). Never rewrite legacy hold/renewal JSON merely to canonicalize it.
canonical_encoding_and_bounds.integer_bounds: PR numbers1..2147483647; revisions0..9007199254740991; version exactly integer1 (receipt version exactly integer2). bool never satisfies an integer field. SHA1 fields exactly40 lowercase hex, SHA256 exactly64 lowercase hex, generation/execution IDs exactly32 lowercase hex. Repository exactly OWNER/REPO, each component1..100 ASCII characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -, no empty/dot/dot-dot component. Branch1..200 ASCII characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / -, neither absolute nor containing an empty/dot/dot-dot path component; no ref normalization. Request ID1..128 ASCII characters A-Z a-z 0-9 : _ -. Thread/producer/job metadata is bounded opaque data, never a path or command to use.
canonical_encoding_and_bounds.budget_enforcement: A bounded iterative exact-type walker checks depth, nodes, strings and aggregate UTF8 lengths before canonical encoding; stop at limit+1, never encode an unbounded object to discover its size. Check every dictionary key is an exact built-in str before sorting/encoding; keys are nodes at the containing object's child depth and consume the same per-string/aggregate UTF8 and node/depth budgets as values, including inside opaque metadata. Track active container identities iteratively and reject cycles; count repeated noncyclic values for each serialized occurrence. Per-argument and total budgets are conjunctive. Full receipt explanations retain the existing maximum12000 characters each, additionally bounded by UTF8/generic limits. Raw SQL TEXT columns use the row/snapshot budgets, not the receipt metadata's65536 string limit. Query known selected keys with LIMIT4097 and stream metadata lengths/types before fetching actual large TEXT cells; enforce per-row, per-table and aggregate budgets before materializing full rows. All columns use literal known schema; no SELECT * or unbounded fetchall. Unexpected BLOB, nonfinite REAL, incompatible schema, overbudget or incomplete collection is typed pending, never truncation, an empty result, authority deletion or automatic limit increase.
canonical_encoding_and_bounds.local_time_and_lock_budget: Checked helper connections use the fixed AGENT_STATE_DIR/review_control.sqlite3, SQLite URI mode=ro for snapshots and mode=rw for mutation, timeout=0 and busy_timeout=0; no waiting30s through legacy connect on either API path. No create/mkdir/chmod/DDL occurs inside either API. Add a trusted SQL progress handler checking a2-second monotonic cooperative deadline every1000 VM instructions and explicit checks between collection phases. A busy writer or expired deadline rolls back and returns typed pending. This is a bounded/cooperative metadata budget, not a hard realtime or IO-kill guarantee. There are no API/network/subprocess calls, sleeps, tests, installs or artifact operations under the transaction. Normal trusted connect's separate additive migration prepares the table only after reviewed operational activation.

scope_contract.public_read_signature: prerequisite_authority_snapshot(repository: str, scope: dict) -> dict; raises CoordinatorAuthorityPending(code) or ValueError, never a successful empty fallback
scope_contract.binding_values: repository/number/candidate_head/task_digest equal scope repository/own values; revision is the held request revision, which may precede the current worker request revision. stage is exactly one of plan, plan-review, plan-resolver, code, publish, prerequisite-check. kind is exactly pr_dev_merge, the existing structured prerequisite-wait kind used even when an item is capture_isolation_active_v1. state_sha256/checkpoint_sha256/prerequisite_review_digest/plan_binding_digest and optional predecessor are SHA256; dev_base SHA1. Unsupported legacy workspace/empty-inventory/migration bindings remain on their existing path and are never silently interpreted as composite checked holds.
review_selection_commitment: Require a complete version2 review receipt, not a numbers-only summary. Verify review.sha256=H(receipt without sha256). The held binding's prerequisite_review_digest is H(the ENTIRE receipt including sha256), exactly the existing Gate.intent formula; do not confuse those two hashes.

Review binding has exactly request_id/head/base/context_digest/plan_sha256, with strict ID/hash types. Its request_id equals held request_id, base equals held dev_base, and H(review.binding) equals held plan_binding_digest. Its head is the reviewed planning/checkpoint head and need not equal own current PR head; do not collapse those distinct identities. The current task digest in the hold is also distinct from a receipt binding's context_digest unless the actual caller separately establishes their relation.

Review prerequisites is a nonempty list of at most16 items. Each has exactly kind,repository,number,target,task_id,branch,anchor_head,anchor_task_digest,required_before,reason,plan_location. Kind is pr_dev_merge or capture_isolation_active_v1, repository matches, target is dev, required_before equals ['code','publication'], task_id matches existing1..128 identifier grammar, branch and anchor hashes follow bounds, reason/location are nonblank and<=12000 characters. No self PR, duplicate PR, unknown kind or unsupported timing. Preserve item order in the hashed receipt, but scope.peers is independently sorted ascending by number.

scope.peers contains EXACTLY one entry for EVERY prerequisite number, no omission/addition/duplicate, same repository implicitly, branch byte-equal to that item's reviewed branch. Current head/task_digest are freshly authenticated peer identities supplied by the trusted caller's ordinary/composite proof; they may legitimately differ from reviewed ancestor anchors and are never asserted equal as a shortcut. No API claim authenticates those external observations.

Before returning an initial snapshot and again under the mutation transaction, the actual own hold row must match the full L(binding). Therefore the supplied full receipt hash is anchored to persisted own authority and its complete selected peer set; a caller cannot omit a reviewed peer just by changing scope.peers or supplying a newly hashed smaller receipt. A legitimate scope removal requires the existing separately reviewed amendment and atomic replacement workflow, never this API.

profile_sources and execution.identity remain hash-bound opaque JSON metadata: bounded by the explicit generic grammar; not interpreted as authority, source availability, reviewer authenticity, protocol support, a pathname, or executable content by this API. Their opaque dictionary keys are intentionally not a new callback/configuration language. profile_sources must be a dict whose only possible top-level key is capture_isolation_active_v1, present iff at least one such item exists, with a nonempty dict value when present. execution outer keys are exactly id,identity,thread_id,events_sha256,result_sha256; identity is a dict, execution IDs/digests are strict, thread_id is nonblank bounded text. Require identity.id=execution.id, identity.plan_binding=review.binding, identity.request_id=held request_id, and thread_id!=identity.planner_thread_id. Full receipt/source/execution provenance and source-hash equality are independently established by the trusted consumer's require_receipt/profile_sources/current source review, not invented in this protected SQLite API.

reassessments has at most16 exact number/reason/amendment_sha256 entries, positive distinct numbers, nonblank bounded reasons and SHA256 digests; review_revision is a strict nonnegative integer. These preserved data do not authorize removing any current selected peer or clearing amendments.
scope_contract.branches: scope.own.branch is supplied from the freshly authenticated own PR head ref and bound by the caller/proof; old holds do not contain that ref and this API cannot reconstruct it from a number. Include all current/historical features and feature_contexts rows for the sorted union of own branch and every receipt-selected peer branch. Omission of a selected branch is impossible because this union is derived internally, never passed as a separate list. Empty feature tables remain explicit absence; enrollment authenticity is not inferred from absence.

literal_authority_snapshot.selected_rows: For the first seven tables, select every row for the exact repository and own number plus ALL derived selected peer numbers, without filtering head, request, digest, age or reason. For the two feature tables select every row for repository and the internally derived branch union, without filtering digest. Never query notifications/token, cursors, attention_hints or assessments as authority. Their data is not this API's decision surface. This API also cannot discover an unknown future security table: its contract is this fixed versioned scope; adding a new authority surface requires a new compatible implementation/review rather than assuming old callers cover it.
literal_authority_snapshot.raw_scalar_encoding: Each cell is a closed two-element tagged array: ['null',null], ['text', exact SQL TEXT], ['integer', canonical signed decimal string], or ['real', Python float.hex() finite canonical string]. No bytes/BLOB/callable. Preserve SQL type, exact TEXT whitespace/escaping, finite REAL value, NULL, empty and zero. No parsing/reformatting of historical JSON cells for CAS. Rows are arrays in the fixed column order, sorted by C(row) bytes, with duplicates retained if legacy nullable keys permit them. Deterministic table order is the literal order above. Unknown/malformed rows relevant to eligibility fail closed; old historical identity strings remain raw observations and are not rewritten to modern hashes.
literal_authority_snapshot.hash_formula: snapshot.version=1; scope_sha256=H(scope); tables contains ALL NINE table records, including [] for absent rows. sha256=H(snapshot without sha256). Schema/table/column absence is unsupported_schema, not the same as a supported table with an empty rows list. Snapshot collection uses one BEGIN read transaction and rolls it back/closes on success or failure, with no authority or schema mutation.
literal_authority_snapshot.schema_validation: Within the SAME read/writer transaction, inspect SQLite's schema catalog (sqlite_schema or its compatible sqlite_master alias) and require an ordinary main-database table for each of the exact nine authority names plus coordinator_checked_renewals: object type=table and a real ordinary-table rootpage, not a view/virtual/shadow stand-in. Verify literal column order, declared types, NOT NULL flags, defaults and PK order against the actual unchanged legacy DDL and additive receipt DDL; legacy NULL allowances remain unchanged, all eight receipt columns are NOT NULL and receipt PK order is repository,number,request,binding_sha256. Reject missing/extra/generated/hidden columns, unexpected foreign keys (the expected schema has none), unsupported metadata or incompatible structure. Verify the receipt transition_sha256 single-column UNIQUE key by actual PRAGMA index_list/index_xinfo metadata: unique, nonpartial, ordinary column transition_sha256 only, no expression/prefix/collation substitution; do not assume an index name. Reject ANY unexpected trigger attached to any of these exact TEN tables in both persistent and connection-local temporary schema catalogs; none is expected by this version. This prevents receipt/authority write side effects, not a claimed detected baseline attack. Ordinary unrelated tables/internal indexes are allowed; do not repair/drop objects or execute their SQL. Unsupported schema is pending unsupported_schema, not empty authority. Reads validate schema and collect rows within one BEGIN; mutation validates and rereads within its single BEGIN IMMEDIATE. SQL progress/byte/time bounds apply to schema metadata too.

eligibility_in_the_control_transaction.common: Eligibility is an additional conjunct after exact raw snapshot equality, not a substitute for CAS. No approvals, historical enrollment rows, receipt or caller boolean overrides a denial. Parse only the known fields needed below, under strict bounds; malformed relevant authority produces pending authority_conflict. All rows are preserved. The API never calls paused(), resume_correction(), recover_feature_publication(), owner-command handlers, or any routine which can consume commands, update pauses or perform GitHub IO.
own_initial: Require exactly ONE own coordinator_holds row across every own request; its request equals held request_id and its binding TEXT equals L(binding). Any additional own hold blocks, even for another request, old head or old revision. Missing/replaced hold is stale_hold. On replay the expected post-state instead requires no own holds.

Any own pauses row or feature_amendments row blocks regardless of recorded head: these are existing PR-wide authority, not stale display labels. An own veto for exact current head blocks. Veto rows for distinct old heads are historical but are still included in raw CAS. NULL/malformed head in a veto cannot be safely classified and blocks.

An own corrections row for exact current head AND exact current task_digest is allowed and preserved: it is the very correction request this renewal must return to planning. Requiring its absence would self-deadlock. A row for another head is historical and allowed/preserved. Same current head with another digest or malformed current identity is a task conflict and blocks. No correction is required to exist: a dependency hold may predate a reviewer finding; the newly written renewal itself establishes the existing fresh-planning barrier.

Existing own coordinator_renewals for OTHER requests are preserved; exact current head/task renewals are earlier planning barriers, not a grant to merge or code and not a reason to prevent another dependency from returning the same own correction to planning. Same-current-head/different-digest entries are task conflicts; distinct old heads are historical. Any malformed relevant record blocks. These rows never compensate for an additional own hold.

For the same own request key, no existing renewal is simplest. If one exists with the exact L(binding) but no checked receipt, fail legacy_outcome: do not fabricate checked proof for a legacy transition. If it has another binding, allow replacing that one legacy summary row ONLY when its parsed request/repository match its SQL key and its strict revision is lower than held revision. Equal/newer revision, malformed binding, or same-current-head/different-task identity blocks. Prior checked receipts are never overwritten; the separate additive receipt retains earlier transition provenance.
peers: For EACH complete receipt-selected peer, any coordinator_holds row blocks regardless of its embedded head/revision/request. Any pauses or feature_amendments row blocks regardless of head. Current-head veto blocks; a well-formed old-head veto is historical. No blanket stale-row deletion or approval substitution is permitted.

A corrections row or any coordinator_renewals row matching that peer's freshly authenticated current head AND task_digest is an active peer replan barrier and blocks. Same current head with another digest is a task conflict and blocks. A well-formed row for a distinct historical head is retained/CAS-protected but does not by itself block this current peer. Do not compare against only the reviewed ancestor anchor and thereby miss a current correction. Unknown/malformed current identities block.

Approvals are all snapshotted, including historical heads, actor and callback. This API does not create, authenticate or independently use them as sufficient positive protected approval: genuine approval/current signed-task/fastCI/dev-merge facts are checked by the caller's full proof, then raw controls are CAS-protected here. Adding/removing/changing any selected approval between snapshot and transition causes stale_authority even if it would appear favorable.

features and feature_contexts are fully snapshotted for the derived branch union. The API does not invent a new enrollment rule or treat a current features row as stronger than historical feature_contexts; existing enrolled_feature(..., digest) deliberately permits retained exact context. The caller must establish the actual applicable machine/App/feature enrollment and current task through the trusted existing provenance path. Any selected enrollment-row change after observation fails raw CAS. Missing provenance outside SQLite remains an external admission failure, not an automatically created enrollment.
eligibility_in_the_control_transaction.old_raw_row_changes: A historical row can be nonblocking when initially observed yet still belongs to the raw CAS. Its insertion/deletion/change after observation invalidates admission. No filtered active-only digest is sufficient. Unselected PR/branch rows do not belong to this bounded SQLite scope; global source/security/freeze/request/jobs facts belong to the separately bound external observation and must not be falsely advertised as covered by this transaction.

caller_binding_contract.values: version exactly1; operation exactly checked-coordinator-renewal-v1; repository/number/request_id/candidate_head/task_digest/dev_base/hold_revision exactly match scope/held binding and explicit public args. request_revision>=hold_revision, request_status one of waiting/running, request_stage exactly prerequisite-check, generation32hex. main_head40hex. Every *_sha256 and plan_receipt_sha256 is64hex, with scope_sha256=H(scope), proof_sha256=explicit proof arg, checkpoint_sha256=held checkpoint_sha256, and plan_receipt_sha256=held prerequisite_review_digest=H(full review receipt). No caller_verified/approved/lock_owned boolean or generic permission field. Unknown fields rejected.
caller_binding_contract.external_meaning: request_row_sha256 is H(the ENTIRE actual SQLite requests row as a dict of every column, including exact value TEXT, not only its decoded payload); external_observation_sha256 binds the caller's retained full immutable observation containing the authenticated own/peer current PR/ref/task/head/base identities, full selected inventory/receipt, dev/main/run/native/receiver/source/profile/runtime/signer/global facts. worker/controller/runtime/global hashes have the full actual source/settings/proof identities defined by the independent positive verifier/activation contract, not a filename or model assertion. proof_sha256 hashes the exact immutable retained proof bytes. This API validates shape/equality and records those identities; it cannot authenticate or reopen those external stores itself.
lock_and_order: Only the reviewed host consumer invokes this local protected API; no source agent tool or public endpoint exposes it. The real consumer must call its actual SupervisorLock.assert_current_owner(), with the existing current-thread ownership check, immediately before and after the synchronous call; it keeps that real lock owned throughout. Do not invent assert_owned(), add an alias or change self_host in this API-only feature. No asserted flag/object from model input stands in for ownership. The API has no dependency on self_host's lock class and makes no false claim to atomically verify it. The separate consumer feature must use the actual lock and prove wrong-thread/no-owner refusal before reaching this API.

Before calling, the host has immutably retained proof/complete raw observation and saved an exact full-row-CAS completion intent binding caller fields. It re-reads the entire request row/revision/status/stage/value and generation, own task/patch/checkpoint/review receipt, current external/global/source/runtime facts, and obtains the protected snapshot. Long GitHub/artifact observations use the existing release/reacquire-and-CAS pattern before this final local section. No remote work occurs inside the API.

After checked commit or replay, the host rechecks the entire request row and all mutable external/global/source/runtime observations before moving the request by full-row CAS into fresh planning/independent review. A new owner answer/cancel, head, checkpoint, source/main/runtime/settings change wins and causes operational wait/recollection; it cannot undo an already committed control transition, which remains a renewed correction barrier. No coder, push, enrollment, dispatch or publication follows on the strength of the old result. Both later code and publication sites require a NEW current complete admission, not this receipt as a durable token.

This API-only feature does not update Gate.transfer/recover_resolution. The separate consumer must require BOTH new version1 snapshot and checked mutation capabilities, explicitly inspect structured success, retain their receipt, and use only exact checked-receipt recovery. An absent/old/incompatible capability stays internal operational wait, with no fallback to renew_coordinator or a numbers-only authority digest. Ordinary unchanged legacy pr_dev_merge consumers retain their prior behavior.

additive_checked_receipt.DDL: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS coordinator_checked_renewals (repository TEXT NOT NULL, number INTEGER NOT NULL, request TEXT NOT NULL, binding_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, transition_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, receipt_json TEXT NOT NULL, receipt_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, created REAL NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(repository,number,request,binding_sha256));
additive_checked_receipt.migration: Append only this CREATE TABLE to normal trusted review_control.connect schema initialization. No existing table/column/row/index or legacy API semantics change, no backfill/adoption of old renewals, no receipt garbage collection. The checked API itself opens only an existing reviewed schema and cannot create/migrate it implicitly; it verifies the ordinary table/NOT NULL/PK/UNIQUE/no-trigger structure through the explicit transaction-local schema contract. New table/version changes the actual private schema; future activation/rehearsal must inspect/review the real schema under a fresh operation plan rather than rely on old50f2/875/426 schema proofs.
additive_checked_receipt.receipt_identity: version1 and operation checked-coordinator-renewal-v1. transition_sha256=H(receipt body without transition_sha256); receipt_json=C(full receipt body) decoded as UTF8; receipt_sha256=H(full receipt body). created is a trusted finite time.time() audit value outside the immutable identity; it is not a permission, expiration or user answer. The SQL key and UNIQUE transition hash bind exactly one checked result to an exact L(binding). The stored caller_binding is complete, bounded and canonical. No raw tokens, notification callbacks, private source files or unbounded proof bytes are stored here; the immutable retained proof and raw snapshots remain in existing separately retained evidence and are addressed by exact hashes.
additive_checked_receipt.no_mutable_receipt: INSERT only after the corresponding own hold/renewal CAS, in the SAME transaction; conflict causes rollback. Never INSERT OR REPLACE, UPDATE or DELETE checked receipts. A malformed row/hash/key, different proof/caller/scope/pre-state for an existing binding key, or unsupported receipt version is a refusal, not a new transition. This additive table is immutable provenance/idempotence bookkeeping, not an additional owner authority or approval table. Other receipts do not themselves grant access; this operation reads its exact key and unique transition identity, not all historic receipts.

checked_mutation_algorithm.public_signature: renew_coordinator_checked(gh, pr, binding, task_digest, *, scope, expected_authority, proof_sha256, caller_binding) -> dict; raises CoordinatorAuthorityPending(code) or ValueError
checked_mutation_algorithm.before_transaction: Validate closed exact types, all budgets and internal hashes. gh.repository must equal scope.repository; pr must be a dict with a strict own number, state='open', head.sha and head.ref matching scope.own (extra authentic GitHub PR response fields are inert). binding equals scope.binding, task_digest equals binding.task_digest, all caller equality constraints hold. expected_authority must be an exact version1 nine-table snapshot for H(scope), with valid raw tags/schema/order/bounds and recomputed sha256. Never accept a hash-only expected value. Do not fetch PRs or execute gh methods here.
transaction_order: Open the existing fixed DB read-write with zero busy wait; BEGIN IMMEDIATE once. Validate transaction-local ordinary-table/column/nullability/PK/receipt-UNIQUE/no-trigger schema for all ten involved tables and read the exact checked receipt by repository/number/request/SHA256(L(binding)). No separate preflight connection gives mutation authority. All exit paths close and roll back on failure; success commits once.

If the checked receipt exists, take only the replay path below. Never retry a first transition or call the legacy API. Otherwise, collect the complete nine-table current raw snapshot in this same transaction; require C(current snapshot)=C(expected_authority), not only a caller-provided digest. This includes explicit absence and every selected historical row. Validate actual exact own held binding plus the complete selected receipt relation again under this writer transaction.

Apply all own/peer eligibility predicates above. Derive the exact expected post-snapshot from that actual pre-snapshot: remove ONLY the one exact own hold row; insert the six-column own coordinator_renewals row (repo, own number, own request, L(binding), own head, own task_digest), or replace ONLY that own same-key older-revision summary row allowed above. Every other cell/table/row is byte/type-identical. Re-sort and recompute post snapshot SHA under the same scope.

Use parameterized INSERT for absent own renewal, or an UPDATE constrained by the exact old six-column values for the permitted older summary, requiring rowcount1. Then DELETE coordinator_holds WHERE repository=? AND number=? AND request=? AND binding=? using exact L(binding), requiring rowcount1. No wildcard release, other-request mutation, pause/correction/amendment/veto/enrollment/approval mutation or legacy renewal call. Recollect actual post-snapshot under the same transaction and require exact equality with the derived post-state.

Build and INSERT the immutable checked receipt with exact pre/post/proof/caller hashes and trusted audit timestamp, requiring success. AFTER that INSERT and BEFORE COMMIT, read back all eight literal columns of the exact stored receipt key and require exact key, transition_sha256, canonical receipt_json, receipt_sha256 and intended finite audit timestamp equality; recompute its canonical hashes and require the intended immutable receipt. Then recollect the actual nine-table authority snapshot and require exact byte/type equality with the already derived expected post-state. These FINAL receipt-and-authority readbacks follow the last write; the earlier pre-INSERT post-state read is not sufficient. Any missing/changed/duplicate/unsupported receipt or post-INSERT authority discrepancy rolls back all three writes. Only then commit together. A failure anywhere, including receipt conflict, budget expiry or injected database error, rolls back renewal update, hold deletion and receipt insertion together. Return the committed closed result only after commit succeeds; an uncertain local commit result is recovered by exact replay, never blind deletion or an assumed rollback.
replay_path: Validate the existing receipt's complete schema, canonical JSON, receipt_sha256, transition hash, SQL key and exact input binding/scope/proof/caller/pre-snapshot identities. Different proof, generation, request revision/status/stage/row hash, checkpoint/patch/head/task/source/runtime/global identity, or expected pre-snapshot is a different call and fails receipt_conflict. Receipt replay is not a way to refresh observations by editing the caller binding.

Derive the expected post-snapshot again from the supplied exact expected pre-snapshot and its permitted own transition. Read the nine-table actual current snapshot under the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE, requiring exact equality with that derived post-state AND its hash equal to the receipt post_authority_sha256. Require no own holds at all and the exact recorded own legacy renewal, and re-evaluate all current relevant eligibility predicates under replay semantics. All peers and unrelated own rows must still equal the expected post-state.

A reinstalled even byte-identical own hold, any replacement/newer/additional hold, new current correction, selected approval/enrollment change or historical selected-row change makes replay stale.
